newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: New Straits Times suspension sparks sales talk.
newsitem.headline: New Straits Times suspension sparks sales talk.

text.p: The suspension of trading of shares in Malaysian media and finance group New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd (NSTP) prompted speculation on Tuesday that it could be selling its 20 percent stake in Commerce Asset Holdings Berhad.
NSTP shares were suspended from trading on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on Tuesday morning for a company announcement.
The company, which is holding its extraordinary general meeting on Tuesday, publishes Malaysia's flagship daily newspaper the New Straits Times.

Trading in stock of infrastructure developer Malaysian Resources Corporation Berhad (MRCB), which owns nearly 10 percent of NSTP stock, was suspended simultaneously. Company officials at MRCB also could not be reached for comment.
Exchange officials did not comment on the share suspensions but said that both New Straits Times and Malaysian Resources Corporation would be making announcements, possibly on Tuesday afternoon.

Analysts said Malaysian telecommunications cable manufacturer FCW Holdings Bhd could be a prime candidate for NSTP's stake in Commerce if it is being sold. FCW Holdings stock was still trading on Tuesday.
"We feel that NSTP is going to be selling its 20 percent stake in Commerce Asset Holdings probably to FCW," said a local analyst who declined to be identified.
No officials from NSTP, FCW or Commerce Asset were available for comment.
Commerce Asset Holdings is a financial supermarket with activities in commercial and merchant banking, as well as stock broking and research.

According to Commerce Asset Holding's latest annual report, the fully paid up share capital of one ringgit shares is 256.6 million ringgit. A 20 percent stake of this at the last-traded price of 16 ringgit amounts to 821 million ringgit.
